findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: The ceiling along the cook-line is observed to have an accumulation of flour on the tiles and light covers. There is observed to be flour coming from the ceiling onto food-contact surfaces and into the batter stations. This is a potential for cross contamination. This violation is still present today. The PIC stated that they are working on cleaning the ceiling. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2026 (combined with the scheduled follow up for violation #47) to ensure that the ceiling along the cook-line has been cleaned to prevent cross contamination to food.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The lemonade nozzle on both soda machines in the facility were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- Both nozzles were cleaned during the inspection and this was discussed with both PICs. Ensure that soda nozzles are being cleaned frequently enough to prevent the accumulation of soil residue.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There are multiple dipping sauces that state to “Keep Refrigerated” that are being held at room temperature. These sauces are stored in the walk-in cooler until they are needed and are stored in a container in the drive-through at room temperature. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that these sauces were placed on the counter at around 9am and the sauces were voluntarily discarded due to being kept past the allowed 4 hours under Time as Control. These sauces will be stored in the bottom of the preparation cooler going forward. Ensure that Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food items are stored at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The walk-in cooler is observed to have an ambient temperature of 46F to 49F. Chicken was probed to be at 48F and 49F. This was discussed with the PIC, who stated that the walk-in cooler was checked at 9am that morning and was at 38F. The chicken that was delivered that morning was moved into the walk-in freezer and the other TCS items that were recently delivered were moved into other coolers. CORRECTED- The following items were probed and voluntarily discarded during the inspection: 
1. 4 pans of chicken (4 bags of classic and 4 bags of boneless): 47F and 48F. 
2. Multiple boxes of sauces, including buttermilk ranch (48F) and 8 boxes of blackened ranch (48F). 
3. Tartar sauce (48F). 
4. 1 box of havarti cheese (47F). 
5. 1 bag of shredded cheddar cheese (47F). 
6. 2 boxes of cabbage (49F). 
All other TCS food items that were within the proper temperature range were moved into another cooler or the walk-in freezer. The PIC stated that there is a company on the way to repair the walk-in cooler. Ensure that other TCS food items are not put into the walk-in cooler until it is properly holding temperature at 41F and below. Ensure that TCS food items are properly cold held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: In the batter stations, raw chicken probed to be at 52F and egg wash probed to be at 56F. The batter stations rely on ice baths for proper cold holding and there was no ice observed underneath the pans of food. The ice machine in the back of the kitchen is not functioning, according to the PIC, and they have to use the lobby ice machine for their ice baths. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that ice had been added under the pans only an hour before this. Ice was added to the water underneath the pans. Egg wash was probed to be at 41F and chicken was probed to be at 39F. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there is always plenty of ice and water to submerge the bottom of the pans to allow for proper cold holding of 41F and below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The walk-in cooler is observed to have an ambient temperature of 46F. There were multiple TCS food items that were discarded (see violation #22). The facility only has one preparation cooler and one standing cooler besides the walk-in cooler. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2026 to ensure that the walk-in cooler has been repaired and is properly cold holding at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: There are single-use boats sitting above the fryer with their food contact surfaces exposed to contamination. Discussed proper single service storage. Ensure that all single-service utensils and articles are inverted to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: According to the PIC, the ice machine in the back of the facility is not functioning and they are waiting on a switch to repair it. Ice baths are used for cold holding for the batter stations and these were observed to not be properly cold holding during today’s inspection (see violation #22). Without the ice machine in the kitchen, they have to rely on the soda machines for ice. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2026 to ensure that the ice machine has been repaired or replaced. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. THIRD REPEAT- The dish shelves across from the ice machine are rusted. The shelves either need to be sealed or replaced to prevent contamination to clean dishes. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The drain of the sanitizer compartment of the triple sink is observed to have an issue where even if it is closed, there is a slow leak coming from it. The facility is using a stopper in place of using the drain handle. Ensure that this issue is repaired to prevent the need for a stopper. The triple sink should be in good repair. 
3. SECOND REPEAT- There is ice build-up on the walk-in freezer pipes on the fan unit. Ensure that this ice is scraped off and that the issue causing the ice build up is repaired. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair or replaced as needed.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of being cleaned: 

1. The walk-in cooler fan covers were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. 
2. The floor in the walk-in cooler is observed to have a spill in the back of it and needs to be cleaned. 
3. The shelves in the walk-in cooler are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. 
4. The mop sink and the walls around it need to be cleaned. There were a few flies observed in this area. Ensure that this area is being cleaned frequently to prevent pest harborage conditions. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are being cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: There are two drains in front of the fryers and batter stations that are observed to not be draining. A follow up is scheduled for 5/21/2026 to ensure that the drains have been repaired and are properly draining. Educate staff to keep drain covers on drains and to prevent grease from going down the drain to avoid future back-ups or cloggings.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. SECOND REPEAT- The front drink station in the drive through is observed to be in need of being sealed to the wall. Ensure that this is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. There are multiple holes in the wall above the handwashing sink behind the batter station. Ensure that these holes are sealed and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
3. The NUDO board is observed to need to be sealed behind the soda syrups and the carbonation tank. 
4. There is coving that is observed to need to be re-sealed to the wall across from the carbonation tank. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. All repairs should be made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
